title: AJK Legislative Assembly Convenes to Elect Gilani as 17th Prime Minister Amid PML-N Revolt
detail: The Azad Jammu & Kashmir Legislative Assembly convened in Muzaffarabad on August 28, 2026 to elect Barrister Syed Iftikhar Ali Gilani as the territory's 17th prime minister, under a schedule fixed by the Speaker's office: nomination papers filed 9:30–10:30am, voting at 2pm following Friday prayers, and the winner's oath-taking at 4pm at the AJK Presidency. PML-N's 32-seat coalition (with allied JUI and Awam Dast-e-Bazu members) against PPP's 14 gave Gilani a clear arithmetic path, but the session proceeded under the shadow of the intra-party revolt that broke out a day earlier: PML-N AJK President Shah Ghulam Qadir, the party's original nominee before Nawaz Sharif switched to Gilani, maintained he would boycott the vote, and former AJK PM Raja Farooq Haider likewise withheld his endorsement. The transition is also proceeding before AJK's four-phase 2026 election is fully complete — voting in seven constituencies across Poonch and Sudhnoti has yet to conclude, leaving roughly a fifth of the territory without directly elected representation as the new government forms, an echo of the 1991 precedent in which Sardar Abdul Qayyum Khan also reached the premiership via a reserved seat.

confidenceReason: Pre-vote reporting on a same-day session; the assembly's PM vote and oath had not yet been confirmed as complete by wire sources at time of writing.

title: Barrister Iftikhar Gilani Elected and Sworn In as AJK's 17th Prime Minister
detail: The Azad Jammu & Kashmir Legislative Assembly elected Barrister Syed Iftikhar Ali Gilani (PML-N) as the territory's 17th prime minister on August 28, 2026, with Gilani securing 30 votes against PPP candidate Sardar Mukhtar Khan's 14, reflecting some abstentions/absences from the 46-seat PML-N-led coalition amid the intra-party revolt led by dropped nominee Shah Ghulam Qadir. AJK's Acting President and Assembly Speaker Chaudhry Tariq Farooq administered the oath of office at a Muzaffarabad ceremony attended by legislative assembly members, political leaders, senior government officials and the public. In his remarks after taking oath, Gilani thanked Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif, PML-N supremo Nawaz Sharif and Punjab CM Maryam Nawaz, and pledged to work for development and prosperity in the territory.

media.caption: Barrister Syed Iftikhar Ali Gilani takes the oath of office as AJK's 17th prime minister, Muzaffarabad, August 28, 2026

title: Pakistani Drones Cross LoC in Rajouri's Nowshera Sector, Army Foils Infiltration Bid
detail: Three suspected Pakistani drones crossed the Line of Control into the Rumlidhara area of the Nowshera sector, Rajouri district, late on the night of August 27-28, 2026; alert Indian Army troops opened fire, forcing the drones to retreat toward Pakistan. A search operation was launched to check for any dropped contraband, arms or narcotics; none had been recovered by evening. Separately on August 28, soldiers in the same general area noticed suspicious movement of a suspected infiltrator along the LoC; the intruder opened fire when challenged, troops retaliated, and the individual is believed to be hiding in the area as a large-scale search operation continues with senior officers monitoring. No casualties were reported in either incident.

title: Two Hand Grenades Recovered During Naka Checking in Baramulla's Kunzer, One Arrested
detail: A joint security party comprising Police Station Kunzer, the Special Operations Group, CRPF's 176 Battalion and the Army's 2 Rashtriya Rifles recovered two hand grenades from a man during naka (checkpoint) checking at Wussan Bangil in Kunzer, north Kashmir's Baramulla district, on August 28, 2026. The suspect, identified as Shakir Nabi Lone of Hardu Aboora, Kunzer, attempted to flee on noticing security personnel but was apprehended on the spot; the grenades were recovered during a personal search. An FIR (No. 115/2026) was registered at Police Station Kunzer and investigation is underway.
